title: Tensor Train fails to approximate complex-valued tensors (error grows with rank)
author: Albly

comments.author: JeanKossaifi
comments.body:
Thank you @Albly for the clear issue and fix! This is a big bug!

A couple of notes: I tend to use the the relative reconstruction error as a metric as it is easily interpretable (`tl.norm(tensor - rec, 2)/tl.norm(tensor)`).

The other thing is that (besides the current bug!), the random tensor is typically full rank and so 1 < rank < 15 is likely to be very low. Which brings me to the last point: I would normally sample tensors using our random module:
```python
tl.random.random_tt(shape=tensor_shape, rank=20, dtype=np.complex128).to_tensor()
```

The issue is that in the complex context, it returns a complex tensor with 0 complex (which is why I suppose tests pass anyway). We could fix it but I feel this shouldn't be our responsibility to handle the core random generation but numpy/pytorch etc should do it however they want.
